gpt.rationale: For residential nonpayment of rent, the landlord must give written notice stating that the rent is in arrears and that the tenancy will terminate unless the tenant pays within five days. The landlord may proceed with eviction only if the tenant fails to pay within that statutory five-day notice period.

gemini.rationale: The statute provides that if rent is unpaid when due and the tenant fails to pay rent within five days after written notice is served, the landlord may terminate the rental agreement and file a complaint for eviction.

federal.effect: During active moratorium periods: 30-day notice required before filing; no fees or penalties for nonpayment during moratorium. federal.name: SCRA § 3951 (Servicemembers Civil Relief Act)
federal.applies_when: Servicemembers and their dependents occupying a residence as their primary dwelling, where the servicemember's military service materially affects their ability to pay the rent.
federal.effect: During a period of military service, a landlord may not evict a servicemember or their dependents from their primary residence without first obtaining a court order. Court may stay proceedings up to 90 days or adjust the rental obligation. Protection applies when monthly rent does not exceed the annual threshold: $4,954.34/month (2024; formula: 130% of BAH for E-5 with dependents, highest BAH area — adjusted annually by DoD). Landlord must file affidavit of non-military-service before default judgment may enter (50 U.S.C. § 3931(b)(1)). FY23 NDAA amendment: replaced CPI-adjusted fixed-dollar threshold with current BAH formula.
federal.statute: 50 U.S.C. § 3951; as amended by Pub. L. 117-263, Div. E, Title LV, § 555 (FY23 NDAA, Dec. 23, 2022)
federal.threshold_formula: 130% of BAH for military member pay grade E-5 with dependents, highest BAH area in the United States (adjusted annually by DoD)

elements_confirmed: A material noncompliance by the landlord with the rental agreement or with the landlord's statutory maintenance obligations exists on the premises.
The noncompliance materially affects the health and safety of the tenant.
The tenant provided the landlord with written notice specifying the breach.
The landlord failed to remedy the breach within twenty (20) days of receiving the written notice.
The tenant raises the landlord's noncompliance as a counterclaim or defense and is prepared to pay any accrued rent into the court registry as ordered.
